question: Did the logo skill cover wordmarks, and was research-router best-practice research performed before the font choice?
skill_scope: Licensed lettering, optical spacing, terminal shapes, small-size and background proof are explicit. Automatic research-router invocation, a detailed typeface-selection rubric and a weight-comparison gate are not explicit.
gaps: Shortlist rationale was subjective and insufficiently documented against the brief.
Each font was shown at only one weight.
Builder uses glyph advance widths plus manual pair gaps; it does not apply OpenType GPOS shaping or compare a default-kerned baseline. This is a process gap, not proof of a visible defect.
User tentative acceptance was treated too much like final approval.
Actual product usage has not been verified.

current_research.date_scope: Foundational professional practice, not recent popularity
current_research.publication_dates: Not recovered; no claim of recent-90-day evidence
current_research.discovery: Two queries returned off-topic/general results; known original URLs used as allowed fallback
current_research.failed_url: https://practicaltypography.com/about.html returned HTTP 404 in provider attempts; not retried

sources.finding: Practical Typography treats fonts as only one part of typography and emphasizes composition; this is author guidance, not a paid-font requirement for naeil.

Practical Typography distinguishes pair kerning from overall letterspacing; its InDesign-specific metrics advice supports comparing the font-defined baseline before our manual adjustments, not prohibiting visual hand-tuning.

Google Design reports defining brand challenges, testing sizes and weights and preparing spacing, clearance and product-lockup specifications for its own identity. This is a case study, not proof Lato is best.
The Lato introduction describes warmth, friendliness and semi-rounded details; this supports a plausible fit to naeil but is self-description, not independent comparative validation.

recommendation: Keep Lato as the leading provisional choice. Next: write explicit criteria, compare a font-defined spacing baseline with hand adjustments and a small weight range, then inspect real placements before final designation. No font or product assets changed during this audit.
